_: The current burn's windows (Burn with no switch; docs/hub/usage.md, "Today and this week"), one row per input the rule distinguishes. Every time is LOCAL, yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, read on the clock of the machine running the suite; weekStarts is the burn.weekStarts value the row is read under -- Friday 05:00 is the shipped default, Monday 09:00 another day and hour. windows: at now, Today starts at local midnight, This week at the latest week start at or before now, and the answer is right until nextBoundary, the sooner of the next midnight and the next week start. records: whether another machine's day record dated <date> counts toward the week starting weekStart -- the week it STARTS in, a record starting at 00:00 on its date, so a record dated the day a week starts on is the week before's (the week starts later that day). summaries: both halves together at one now -- this machine's lines (t is the offset from now's local midnight) split at the week's start exactly, another machine's record dated the week's first day in Today and not in This week, and this machine's own record never read. weekStartsValues: what Config -Set burn.weekStarts accepts (as it reads back) and refuses. Asserted by tkTestToolkit -Burn.

windows.name: a Wednesday: the week began the Friday before
a Thursday night: the next boundary is midnight
Friday 04:59: still last week, and the boundary is at 05:00
Saturday: the week began the day before
Monday 09:00, on a Wednesday: the week began on Monday
Monday 09:00, Monday 08:59: still last week, the boundary at 09:00
Monday 09:00, Monday 09:00 exactly: the week starts
Sunday 00:00: the week starts with the day, so the boundary is that midnight

rows.why: the Thursday before: the week before's
the Friday the week starts on: its record starts at 00:00, five hours before the week
the Friday the week ends on: its record starts at 00:00, inside the week
Monday 09:00: the Monday the week starts on, nine hours before the week
Monday 09:00: the Monday the week ends on
Sunday 00:00: a week starting at midnight takes its own day's record
Sunday 00:00: the next Sunday is the next week's
